slice03_followups: All three addressed. (1) TRIMMING: the primitive already trims - combobox.tsx commitCreate calls onCreate?.(query.trim()) and createRowLabel trims for the label too. Trimming belongs in the primitive, not the call site, because the create row's visible text and the committed value must agree and only the primitive owns both. Locked with a new test in combobox.test.tsx, 'hands onCreate the trimmed query, not the raw input value': types '  Maria  ', asserts the row reads exactly '+ Criar novo contato "Maria"', asserts the search field still holds the untrimmed '  Maria  ' (so the trim is at the boundary, not a mutation of what the operator typed), then commits and asserts onCreate('Maria') and that onChange was not called. The adoption layer has its own version, 'trims the surrounding whitespace out of the create query', which proves it end to end through the cliente picker. (2) PINNED FOOTER POSITIVE CONTROL: added to combobox.test.tsx test 10 - the bare closest(...)===null is now accompanied by scrollArea.contains(createRow())===false plus the positive half scrollArea.contains(row(0))===true, so the assertion fails if the scroll area stops existing or if no row is inside it. The adoption test carries the same pair, and while writing it I found that the bare closest() form is in fact CONFOUNDED at the call sites: the wizard body is itself overflow-y-auto, so closest('.overflow-y-auto') finds the dialog and passes for the wrong reason. The adoption test therefore scopes the query to the panel via listbox().querySelector('.overflow-y-auto'). Worth flagging as the reason the primitive's original assertion looked stronger than it was. (3) DISABLED WHILE OPEN: reachable at exactly one of my call sites, the wizard Finder picker (disabled={sellerIsFinder}), toggled by the separate 'Vendedor e o finder desta venda' button; also structurally reachable at LinkGeneratorForm's product picker (disabled={!appId}). It is a non-issue in a real browser because a pointer click fires mousedown before click and the primitive's document mousedown listener dismisses the panel first. Rather than document that, I locked it: the new test 'dismisses an open picker when the control that disables it is clicked' opens the Finder panel, dispatches a realistic mousedown+click pair on the toggle, and asserts the listbox is gone and the trigger is now disabled. No primitive change was needed, so slice 03's API stayed frozen.

remediation: Gate 2 attempt 1 blocked on one false sentence in CLAUDE.md, not on code. The old text read "Every single-select picker in `apps/web/src` uses `Combobox` from `@/components/ui/combobox`." That is demonstrably false: apps/web/src/admin/products/ProductDialog.tsx:132 (product status) and apps/web/src/admin/products/CommissionRuleForm.tsx:94 (commission basis) still use the shadcn Radix Select. I had written an explicit `in apps/web/src` scope while carving nothing out. No code changed; only CLAUDE.md. The `## UI Controls` section now splits the one overloaded claim into three true ones. (1) The ban, stated app-wide because it genuinely is: "Native `<select>`, `<option>` and `<datalist>` are banned everywhere in `apps/web/src`, and `no-restricted-syntax` in `apps/web/eslint.config.js` fails lint if one comes back." plus a sentence saying why, so the next agent gets the intent and not just the prohibition. (2) The Combobox mandate, scoped to exactly where it holds: "Every single-select picker in `apps/web/src/sales-ops/**`, plus the workspace switcher in `apps/web/src/auth/react.tsx` and every data-driven picker in the legacy `admin/**` and `finder/**` trees, uses `Combobox` from `@/components/ui/combobox`. It is the only searchable picker in the app." (3) The exception, named with file paths, reason and an expiry instruction: "Documented exception, and the only one: `apps/web/src/admin/products/ProductDialog.tsx` (product status) and `apps/web/src/admin/products/CommissionRuleForm.tsx` (commission basis) keep the shadcn `Select`. Both are two-option closed enums that never grow, so search buys nothing, and a Radix `Select` is not a browser-native picker, so both already satisfy the ban above. Convert them to `Combobox` whenever those two screens are next worked on, and do not add a third such site." Every claim was re-verified by grep before committing: zero `<select>`/`<option>`/`<datalist>` in production source; zero `<Select` in sales-ops/**; the workspace switcher and both data-driven legacy pickers import Combobox; exactly two `<Select` sites remain and both are in admin/products; and each of those two really has exactly two SelectItem children, read directly rather than counted, so the "two-option closed enum" reason is accurate and not assumed. I also caught and fixed a self-inflicted contradiction while drafting: my first pass opened with "No browser-native picker anywhere in `apps/web/src`", which contradicts the pre-existing bullet three lines below it stating that `<input type="date">` is the one browser-native picker still allowed. Scoping the opening bullet to the three banned element names removes the contradiction and keeps the date exception the single, explicit carve-out it was. One further wording correction: I first justified the exception as "in a frozen legacy tree", but this same slice edits both of those files' siblings (the ProductDialog app picker and LinkGeneratorForm), so "frozen" would have misled the next agent into thinking the files are untouchable. The reason now given is the true one, that the enums never grow so search buys nothing.
